name: multiscale-bioprocess
title: v2ecoli — Bioprocess Migration & Reactor Coupling
description:
Migrates and enhances v2ecoli for bench-scale bioprocess context, then
couples it to `vivarium-collective/pbg-bioreactordesign` for the physical
reactor side.

**Scope.** Internal v2ecoli upgrades (time-varying environment, population
aggregation, reactor coupler) plus a coupling adapter — not a reactor
wrapper built from scratch; reactor physics comes from
`pbg-bioreactordesign` consumed as a dependency. Out of scope: dynamic-FBA
as the cell side (the upstream multiscale-bioprocess roadmap's choice, see
references/expert/multiscale_bioprocess_roadmap.md); multi-cell colony
composite as the primary path (deferred); CFD / spatial-mixing;
WCM-internal mass-balance audits.

**Fed-batch is deferred.** `pbg-bioreactordesign` does not yet expose
fed-batch operations (feed schedules, dynamic volume), so until that lands
upstream or a v2ecoli-side feed Step is added, the mbp-05 Beulig benchmark
scopes to the batch portion of the dataset; the spec PR makes that scope
call explicit. Adding fed-batch is expected to be a top-priority mbp-06 gap.

**Reactor + coupling code lives in `v2ecoli/`** (planned packages
`v2ecoli.composites.ecoli_time_varying_env`,
`v2ecoli.composites.ecoli_population`,
`v2ecoli.composites.reactor_bird_coupled`); the cell-side composite stays
`v2ecoli.composites.ecoli_baseline` (single cell + Division Step).
`pbg-bioreactordesign` is added as a workspace dependency in mbp-03.

Studies, in dependency order (current `phase` shown; multi-axis status is
canonical per each study.yaml):

1. mbp-01-time-varying-environment — **Evaluate phase** — media /
   environment becomes externally driven (time-varying nutrient pool
   consumed by the existing Layer-1 Steps); plumbing + qualitative-extreme
   tests only (chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §3), with gradient-shape /
   quantitative-biology deferred to the `transport-kinetics-fidelity`
   candidate-future-study.
2. mbp-02-population-aggregation — **Evaluate phase** — aggregates per-cell
   mass into reactor-scale biomass / OD600 / cell-count via
   `cells_per_agent` representative-sampling scaling
   (chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §4; Eran's choice over literal-sum to make
   240-min batch dynamics resolvable). OD600 is cosmetic;
   `biomass_concentration_gL` is canonical.
3. mbp-03-bird-reactor-coupling — adapter to `pbg-bioreactordesign`'s
   **BiRDTransportProcess** (a transport-only sibling of
   `BiRDReactorProcess` with no internal biomass ODE; see
   `chris_feedback_2026_05_26.md` §5 for the Option-B rationale). BiRD owns
   transport physics, v2ecoli owns biomass; the keystone coupling, and the
   first impl PR to wire a real engine under the cell-side interface
   contract (`references/expert/cell_side_interface_contract.md`).
   **Cross-investigation dependency:** mbp-03 entering Build is gated on the
   upstream `pbg-bioreactor-transport-fork` PR landing in pbg-bioreactordesign
   (seeded as a candidate-future-study in mbp-06).
4. mbp-04-multigeneration-runs — sustained coupled run (≥ 3 v2ecoli
   generations); mass-balance audit; regime transition into
   substrate-limited growth.
5. mbp-05-palsson-benchmark — evaluation phase
   (`chris_feedback_2026_05_26.md` §10) rendering a structured comparison
   report (overlay panels + categorized divergences) against the Beulig
   2025 (mSystems; senior author Palsson) batch-phase prefix. Pass criteria
   are whether the comparison was executed and reported coherently, not
   whether biology matched within tolerance; divergences feed mbp-06's gap
   analysis as input.
6. mbp-06-gap-analysis — evaluation phase, not construction: walks the
   mbp-01..05 artifacts, synthesizes gaps across five axes (v2ecoli biology
   / coupling / BiRD physics / Beulig scope / methodology), and feeds the
   next investigation iteration.
7. mbp-07-millard-kinetic-metabolism — Evaluate phase — kinetic-metabolism
   (Millard 2017) drop-in cell engine (baseline_millard) + reactor coupling,
   validated against the FBA baseline and graded head-to-head against the
   Beulig WT batch prefix alongside the WCM-FBA and iML1515 arms (3-arm
   report cards).
lead:
This investigation lifts v2ecoli's single-cell whole-cell model into a
bench-scale bioreactor and holds it up against the Beulig 2025 (mSystems;
senior author Palsson) high-density E. coli study. The work is internal
v2ecoli upgrades (time-varying environment, population aggregation, a
reactor coupler) plus a coupling adapter to pbg-bioreactordesign, not a
reactor built from scratch; reactor physics is consumed as a dependency.
Per the 2026-05-26 reviewer reframe (chris_feedback §1 + §10) success is
defined as "comparison harness built and applied; structured gap inventory
produced," not "Palsson benchmark achieved": every biological divergence
feeds mbp-06 as evidence rather than a knob to tune. Studies are gated in
dependency order; mbp-03 (the keystone BiRD coupling) is now unblocked by
the upstream transport-fork merge.

studies.mbp-01-time-varying-environment:
Time-varying environment hook: v2ecoli's medium becomes externally
driven (EnvironmentDriver → EnvironmentMirror → boundary.external).
Plumbing + qualitative-extreme tests only; build complete (6/6).

studies.mbp-02-population-aggregation:
Population aggregation: per-cell mass → reactor-scale
biomass_concentration_gL via cells_per_agent representative-sampling
scaling (OD600 cosmetic). cpa scaling validated empirically across
seeds (9 orders of magnitude, narrow log-y ribbons). Build complete.

studies.mbp-03-bird-reactor-coupling:
The keystone coupling: adapter to pbg-bioreactordesign's
BiRDTransportProcess (Option B, transport-only, biomass-as-input).
BiRD owns transport physics, v2ecoli owns biomass. Now unblocked: the
upstream pbg-bioreactor-transport-fork merged to main (f40f82f).

studies.mbp-04-multigeneration-runs:
Sustained coupled run (≥3 v2ecoli generations); carbon/O2 mass-balance
audit; regime transition into substrate-limited growth.

studies.mbp-05-palsson-benchmark:
Evaluation phase: renders a structured sim-vs-Beulig comparison report
(overlay panels plus categorized divergences) on the WT batch-phase
prefix. Success = comparison executed and reported coherently, not
tolerance-matched biology; divergences feed mbp-06.

studies.mbp-06-gap-analysis:
Evaluation and synthesis: walks mbp-01..05 artifacts, inventories gaps
across five axes (v2ecoli biology / coupling / BiRD physics / Beulig
scope / methodology), each with a resolution type and venue, feeding
the next investigation iteration.

studies.mbp-07-millard-kinetic-metabolism: Build->Validate->Compare (consolidated): replace v2ecoli's central-carbon FBA with the Millard 2017 kinetic ODE as a drop-in cell engine (baseline_millard), validate it recovers growth vs the FBA baseline, then couple it to the BiRD reactor and grade it head-to-head against the Beulig WT batch prefix alongside the WCM-FBA and iML1515 genome-scale FBA arms (3-arm report cards). Deliverables: baseline_millard + reactor_bird_coupled_millard + 3-arm Beulig comparison.

blocked:
Reaching the Beulig high-density regime (~50–80 gDW/L fed-batch endpoint,
or even the ~9.6 g/L batch peak) is out of scope this round. It needs a
both-daughters population-runner architecture plus fed-batch operations,
both deferred to mbp-06 candidate-future-studies. mbp-05 reports the gap;
it does not try to close it.
Strain-specific (SGKO×31 / TRP / TRPp / MEL), transcriptional-state, and
resistance/persistence axes of the Beulig dataset are deferred to mbp-06
or future iterations (see beulig_benchmark_axes below).

glossary.definition:
Grams dry weight per litre, the canonical population biomass observable,
aggregated from per-cell mass listeners × cells_per_agent / reactor volume.

Representative-sampling scaling factor by which one simulated lineage
stands in for cpa real cells under the 0D well-mixed assumption, letting a
single-cell simulation reach reactor-scale biomass without spatial detail.

Volumetric oxygen mass-transfer coefficient (1/h) setting how fast the
reactor replenishes dissolved O2, with a geometry-aware default upstream
(Van't Riet for stirred tanks).

Batch is fixed initial medium with no feeding (the Beulig batch phase
peaks at ~9.6 g/L); fed-batch feeds substrate over time to reach the
~50–80 gDW/L headline density and is not yet exposed upstream (deferred).

O2 concentration in the liquid phase; the shared store where reactor
transport (+) and cell consumption (−) net out as additive deltas.

biological_story:
A whole-cell model simulates one E. coli cell in molecular detail; a
bioreactor runs 10^12–10^13 cells per litre under a changing physical
environment — depleting glucose, oxygen-transfer-limited dissolved O2,
accumulating acetate and CO2. This investigation asks whether the
single-cell model can be lifted into that bench-scale context and held up
against a real published high-density run (Beulig 2025, mSystems; senior
author Palsson). The biology is multi-scale: a single lineage's nutrient
uptake and growth must aggregate into population-scale biomass, which then
draws down the shared medium and consumes oxygen faster than the reactor
can transfer it, driving substrate- and O2-limited growth. v2ecoli already
exposes the right surfaces (Layer-1 media/exchange Steps, per-cell mass
listeners), so the enhancements are additive: an externally driven
environment (mbp-01), a representative-sampling population aggregator
(mbp-02), and a coupler to the reactor's transport physics (mbp-03).

The central result so far is a scale gap, not a tuning failure. v2ecoli's
single-lineage population plateaus at ~4.3 mg/L while the Beulig batch
phase peaks at ~9.6 g/L (max OD ~28 × 0.34 gDW/OD), a ~3.3-order gap not
closable by run duration or a division-flag flip. True both-daughters
accumulation (2^N cells after N generations) needs a population-runner
architecture distinct from the current single-lineage runner, and reaching
the paper's 50–80 gDW/L additionally needs fed-batch operations. The
investigation was therefore reframed (2026-05-26) from "match Beulig within
tolerance" to "build the comparison harness and produce a structured gap
inventory": every biological divergence becomes evidence feeding mbp-06,
not a knob to turn.
question:
Can v2ecoli be migrated and enhanced to run inside a bench-scale
bioreactor? The pieces are a time-varying external-environment hook, a
population aggregator with representative-sampling scaling, and a coupling
adapter to `pbg-bioreactordesign`'s BiRDTransportProcess; the test is a
structured sim-vs-published comparison report (overlay panels plus
divergence triage feeding mbp-06 gap analysis) against the WT batch-phase
prefix of the 2025 Beulig/Palsson mSystems study.

Reframed 2026-05-26 per chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §1 + §10: the original
"reproduces ... within per-metric tolerances" framing built the
tune-to-tolerance impulse into the test design. Success is now defined as
"comparison harness built and applied; structured gap inventory produced,"
not "Palsson benchmark achieved" — all biological divergences feed mbp-06
as evidence.
hypothesis:
Yes, with scope caveats. v2ecoli's Layer-1 Steps (`media_update`,
`exchange_data`) already expose the environment-coupling surface and the
metabolism Process already emits `external_exchange_fluxes`, so the
enhancements are small and additive: (1) a time-varying-env hook over the
existing static-medium plumbing, (2) a population aggregator whose
`cells_per_agent` representative-sampling scaling derives reactor-scale
biomass / OD from per-cell mass listeners, (3) a ReactorCellCoupler Step
bridging to `pbg-bioreactordesign`'s BiRDTransportProcess (transport-only
fork, no internal biomass ODE by construction — the Option-B decision in
chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §5). Each study's acceptance tests gate its impl
PR, the multi-generation coupled run checks that no piece drifts over time,
and mbp-05's evaluation phase renders the comparison report against Beulig
batch-phase trajectories.

Scope caveat: Beulig 2025 reached 50–80 gDW/L (~10^12 – 10^13 cells/L),
which v2ecoli's single-cell-with-Division population cannot reach by
literal-sum aggregation — hence the `cells_per_agent` scaling factor
(mbp-02; representative-sampling under the 0D well-mixed assumption) that
lets the simulated lineage stand in for a larger population. mbp-05 is an
evaluation phase rendering overlays plus categorized divergences rather
than asserting tolerance-based agreement with Beulig, bounding the AI-agent
scope to "execute and report" rather than "tune until match"; mbp-06's gap
analysis is expected to surface a coarse-grained surrogate engine (under
the same cell-side interface contract) as a top-priority follow-up.

executive.what_is_this: Puts the v2ecoli single-cell model inside a bench-scale bioreactor. Seven studies build up the coupling: a time-varying environment hook, population aggregation with representative-sampling scaling, BiRD reactor coupling, multigeneration runs, a sim-vs-Beulig comparison, gap analysis, and a Millard 2017 kinetic-metabolism drop-in with 3-arm Beulig report cards.

`pbg-bioreactor-transport-fork` PR; that fork merged (f40f82f,

shared venv also ships a bigraph_schema older than the worktree's

needing a bigraph_schema>=1.4.3 shadow to `import v2ecoli` at all.

reactor-coupled studies are reproducible without a PYTHONPATH shadow.

new_empirical_evidence.title: mbp-05 preliminary expectation-setting — empirical plateau diagnostic
new_empirical_evidence.finding:
Refined and empirically confirmed 2026-05-29 after pulling the
digitized Beulig batch trajectories from
references/papers/palsson-2025-supp/ (req-1-palsson-ingestion
fully resolved) and running v2ecoli cpa=1e9 for 175 sim-min
(salvaged from a 6h run killed at the system's 128 GB memory
ceiling, enough for the architectural diagnostic).

Beulig batch phase peaks at ~9.6 g/L (max OD ~28 × 0.34) at
~13 h batch elapsed. The 50-80 g/L figure from the paper's
abstract is the fed-batch endpoint, not the batch endpoint;
the earlier charts 00 and 01 used that as their target band
and have been demoted to companion-charts, and chart 02 is now
load-bearing.

v2ecoli at cpa=1e9 under single_daughters plateaus at ~4.3 mg/L.
The biomass oscillates 1.17–4.31 mg/L following the division
cycle (cell_mass 1097→2338 fg, halve at division) but does not
accumulate across generations under this configuration. The
175-min run confirmed this empirically. Gap to Beulig batch
peak under single_daughters: 3.3 orders of magnitude, not
closable by duration alone.

Revised caveat (2026-05-29, empirically tested):
I initially attributed the plateau to single_daughters alone
and predicted --no-single-daughters would accumulate
exponentially. Chart 03 (90-sim-min --no-single-daughters run)
refutes that prediction: both runs peak at the same ~4 mg/L
plateau. The runner's internal log line `gen 2 → following
agent 00 at tick 2501` reveals the actual root cause:
`run_multigen_parquet` simulates both daughters at division
moments but then follows one lineage for continued simulation
and parquet emission. The --no-single-daughters flag flips the
composite-level division behavior but does not change the
runner's emit pattern, so the architectural cap persists
under either config.

True both-daughters accumulation (2^N cells after N gens)
requires a population-runner architecture distinct from
run_multigen_parquet, a new mbp-06 candidate-future-study.
Closing the Beulig batch gap (~9.6 g/L) requires that
population runner plus fed-batch operations together, not just
a config flip.

mbp-05's comparison harness will surface both configurations
diagnostically; it does not try to tune the gap away (Chris's
2026-05-26 §10 execute-and-report reframe).

scientific_argument.main_claim:
v2ecoli can be additively enhanced (time-varying environment +
representative-sampling population aggregation + a BiRDTransportProcess
coupler) to operate inside a bench-scale bioreactor and render a
structured, reviewable sim-vs-published comparison, with the gap to the
Beulig high-density regime attributed to population-runner architecture
and fed-batch operations (surfaced as gaps) rather than tuned away.
evidence_for: mbp-01 advanced from 1 passing / 5 skipped to 6 passing / 0 skipped; the EnvironmentDriver → EnvironmentMirror → boundary.external propagation chain runs at multi-generation scale (commit 60cdbd3).

mbp-02 cells_per_agent scaling validated empirically across seeds {0,1,2} and cpa ∈ {1, 1e6, 1e9}, with log-y parallelism over 9 orders of magnitude and narrow variance ribbons; the per-cell-mass-invariant chart confirms the aggregator never touches per-cell state.
The mbp-03 hard prerequisite is satisfied. pbg-bioreactor-transport-fork merged to pbg-bioreactordesign main (f40f82f, PR
The mbp-05 comparison harness renders sim-vs-Beulig overlays plus categorized divergences from a YAML comparison_overlays list (13 overlays), so adding a comparison is configuration, not code.

evidence_for.The keystone mbp-03 coupling is demonstr: 6 passed, 1 skipped. The full coupled composite produces a physically consistent 0D trajectory — DO rises to Henry saturation with no cells, drops below it under cell O2 demand (cstar_o2=6.58 mg/L, DO 2nd-half mean 6.24 mg/L at 310.15 K), higher kLa raises steady-state DO, one generation completes without divergence, and the O2 mass balance closes within ±5%.

evidence_for: The upstream O2-saturation temperature-sign bug (pbg-bioreactordesign#2) is FIXED and verified. PR
evidence_against: Single-lineage population plateaus at ~4.3 mg/L vs the Beulig batch peak ~9.6 g/L, a ~3.3-order gap not closable by duration or the --no-single-daughters flag (chart 03 refuted that prediction); needs a both-daughters population runner plus fed-batch.

Whether an alternative kinetic metabolism (Millard FBA-bridge / dFBA) adapts better to these conditions is untested under coupling. The bridge is open-loop today (env→metabolism coupling deferred); scoped as the next study.

evidence_against.The CO2 leg of the mbp-03 coupler is wir: in M9-minimal-glucose FBA v2ecoli reports zero CO2 environmental efflux, so cells cannot raise dissolved CO2 above saturation. It needs an overflow/anaerobic condition to test (deferred, not a wiring failure).

key_figures: studies/mbp-02-population-aggregation/charts/04_population-scaling-variance-bands.svg — cpa scaling robust across 3 seeds × 3 cpa (mean ± std, log-y).
studies/mbp-05-palsson-benchmark/charts/02_v2ecoli_vs_beulig_batch_actual.svg — the load-bearing plateau diagnostic (v2ecoli ~4.3 mg/L vs Beulig batch ~9.6 g/L).
caveats: mbp-05/mbp-06 are evaluation phases (chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §10) that execute-and-report, deliberately not tolerance-based biology claims.
Scope is the batch portion of the Beulig dataset only; fed-batch operations are not yet exposed by pbg-bioreactordesign and are deferred (expected top-priority mbp-06 gap).
cells_per_agent is representative sampling under a 0D well-mixed assumption; it lets one simulated lineage stand in for a larger population and does not model spatial heterogeneity.

studies.name: mbp-01-time-varying-environment
studies.question:
Can v2ecoli's `media_update` / `exchange_data` Layer-1 Steps consume an
externally-driven, time-varying nutrient pool — instead of the static
media configuration baked into ParCa — such that metabolic exchange
fluxes and growth rate respond correctly to declining glucose, declining
DO, and other dynamic external concentrations?

studies.name: mbp-02-population-aggregation
studies.question:
Can v2ecoli aggregate single-cell-plus-Division output into population-
level biomass observables (total gDW, cell count) that are physically
meaningful at the reactor scale (OD ≫ 1) — using a **representative-
sampling scaling factor (`cells_per_agent`)** so the simulated lineage
legitimately stands in for an N-cell population under the 0D
well-mixed assumption — and consume population-level signals (e.g.
reactor liquid volume) to maintain correct concentrations?

studies.name: mbp-03-bird-reactor-coupling
studies.question:
Can v2ecoli (with the mbp-01 time-varying-env hook and mbp-02 population
aggregator) be coupled to `pbg-bioreactordesign`'s BiRDReactorProcess —
via a thin adapter that resolves the biomass-ownership conflict between
the two — such that BiRD supplies dissolved O2, kLa, gas-phase physics,
and v2ecoli supplies population biomass and exchange-flux demand,
producing a physically consistent coupled trajectory in a 0D
well-mixed bench-scale reactor?

studies.name: mbp-04-multigeneration-runs
studies.question:
Does the mbp-03 coupled composite (v2ecoli ↔ pbg-bioreactordesign) stay
mass-conserving, computationally tractable, and physically coherent
over multiple v2ecoli generations (3+ doublings) under sustained
reactor dynamics — capturing the regime transition from glucose-replete
exponential growth into glucose-limited or DO-limited slowdown as the
population grows and consumes the batch?

studies.name: mbp-05-palsson-benchmark
studies.question:
Configured with operating conditions matched to the 2025 Palsson lab
high-density E. coli study, does the v2ecoli ↔ pbg-bioreactordesign
coupled model **render a structured comparison report** (sim-vs-
published overlays + categorized divergences + open questions) on
the published WT batch-phase prefix trajectories, suitable to feed
mbp-06's gap-analysis synthesis?

Investigation-level note: the original question framing ("match within
tolerance") was reframed 2026-05-26 to "render a structured comparison."
The success definition is whether the comparison was EXECUTED AND
REPORTED COHERENTLY, not whether biology matched. All biological
divergences feed mbp-06 unchanged.

studies.name: mbp-06-gap-analysis
studies.question:
After mbp-01..05 have produced their per-study findings, what are the
remaining gaps (in v2ecoli's biology coverage, the coupling layer, the
pbg-bioreactordesign physics, and the Beulig benchmark scope) that
prevent the investigation from answering its overarching question, and
how should those gaps be prioritized as the next investigation
iteration (mbp-* round 2, or a sibling investigation)?

studies.name: mbp-07-millard-kinetic-metabolism
studies.question:
The Millard kinetic-metabolism arc, end-to-end. Can the Millard 2017
kinetic central-carbon ODE replace v2ecoli's constraint-based central-
carbon FBA as a drop-in cell engine under the cell-side interface
contract?

Three linked questions:
  1. BUILD     — does the swapped composite (baseline_millard) build and
                 run, with non-trivial live central fluxes (kinetic ODE
                 active, not FBA)?
  2. VALIDATE  — does the Millard whole-cell model recover growth
                 comparable to the FBA baseline, and (once the Millard
                 cell exposes mass-exchange accounting) close mass
                 conservation?
  3. COMPARE   — coupled to the same BiRD reactor and run against the
                 Beulig WT batch prefix, does the Millard kinetic central
                 metabolism track the bioreactor (growth, substrate, gas
                 transfer) BETTER than v2ecoli's WCM-FBA — and how do both
                 compare to the iML1515 genome-scale FBA (Palsson)?
                 Rendered as a structured 3-arm report-card comparison
                 (per-group axis verdicts + categorized divergences),
                 NOT a tolerance gate (execute-and-report, per
                 chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §10).
